title: Cap. VIII Arg. 9: syllogism — no one ordained to eternal punishment without precognition of cause
pass_a_gloss: Unto eternal punishment, says he, no one is ordained by a just Judge without precognition of the cause. But every reprobate is deputed unto punishment by God the just Judge: Therefore not except from the foresighted evil use of free will about to last unto the end. Which is the same as if he had said with the Jesuits and Arminians, not except from foresighted unbelief and disobedience.
pass_b_english: To eternal punishment, he says, no one is ordained by a just Judge without precognition of the cause. But every reprobate is deputed to punishment by God the just Judge. Therefore only from foresighted evil use of free will lasting to the end — which is the same as saying with Jesuits and Arminians: only from foresighted unbelief and disobedience.
source_text: Ad poenam aeternam, inquit, nullus ordinatur a justo Judice sine praecognitione causae. Sed omnis reprobatus est ad poenam a Deo justo Judice deputatus: Ergo non nisi ex praeviso malo usu liberi arbitrii ad finem usque duraturo. Quod idem est ac si dixisset cum Jesuitis et Arminianis, non nisi ex praevisa infidelitate et inobedientia.
